answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public, slashable bond before it may post claims or earn rewards. If several identities coordinate to fabricate consensus, auditors can challenge their claims against signed interaction records; proven fraud burns the bond and forfeits pending rewards. This makes a sybil swarm costly rather than free: the attacker must acquire and immobilize capital for every identity, and risks losing it. A haven or oasis of cheap compute is no escape; the crystal-clear cost is tied to identities, not machines.
